eq. 2.7 (p. 34) uses Bias(fhat(x_0)); the book defines bias verbally
(the error from approximating a real-life problem by a simpler model).
The formula E[fhat(x_0)] - f(x_0) is the standard definition, not one
the book states. The estimator-bias definition of the sds estimation page
(Morrison-Lab/sds, _subfiles/estimation/_def-bias.qmd) is the same idea
with a fixed estimand in place of f(x_0).
-->
:::{#def-prediction-bias}
#### Bias of a prediction

Let $f$ be a fixed function, and let $x_0$ be a point.
Let $\hat f(x_0)$ be a [prediction](expectation.qmd#def-prediction) of the value $f(x_0)$.
The prediction $\hat f(x_0)$ is a random variable,
because it depends on the random training data.
The **bias** of $\hat f(x_0)$ is

$$\bias{\hat f(x_0)} \eqdef \E{\hat f(x_0)} - f(x_0)$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-prediction-bias}
#### Computing the bias of a prediction

Suppose $f(x_0) = 10$,
and the predictions $\hat f(x_0)$,
over repeated training sets,
average $11$.
Then $\bias{\hat f(x_0)} = 11 - 10 = 1$.
The squared bias is $1^2 = 1$,
the value in @exr-prediction-error.

:::
